explanatory_strength.rationale: Owner-earnings story is straightforward: subscription software converting to $9.85B free cash flow with light maintenance capex ($179M), 96% subscription revenue mix, and large buybacks ($11.28B). Franchise quality is high; the open question is whether reinvestment into Firefly/AI preserves owner cash growth or only defends share.

evidence_sufficiency.rationale: FY2025 FCF, shares, RPO, cash, debt, and SBC are filing-reconciled with decision-grade proofs. Quality of earnings is strong on cash conversion, but segment FCF is allocated by revenue weight, management_facts is empty, and incremental AI spend (~$850M reserved in proofs) lacks a verified attach-rate bridge.

downside_control.rationale: Balance sheet can fund the franchise through a de-rating: $5.4B cash versus ~$6.2B long-term debt after the 2025 note issuance. Equity risk is multiple and growth, not solvency. Contract low $350/sh still implies large paper loss from $234.74; buybacks partly debt-funded raise the bar for sustained FCF.

return_vs_alternatives.rationale: Paying ~10× FY2025 owner cash for a high-quality compounder can work if mid-teens growth persists, but contract base return 15.81% is only hurdle-clearing, while Lawrence 32% embeds optimistic growth/exit. Versus other quality reinvestment names, Adobe is not uniquely cheap once AI defense spend and SBC are respected.

claims.claim: FY2025 free cash flow of $9.85B ($23.07/sh) came from $10.03B operating cash flow less $179M capex, evidencing high owner-earnings conversion on a subscription base.

Capital return was aggressive: $11.28B share repurchases in FY2025 while long-term debt rose to about $6.21B and cash fell to about $5.43B, so equity stub quality depends on FCF staying ahead of buyback and SBC claims.
At $234.74, contract base value $656/sh implies 15.81% annualized return (bear/high band 5.87%/22.93%), clearing a ~15% hurdle only in the base capitalization case.

strongest_counter_explanation: This is a classic wonderful business at a fair price: RPO and H1 FY2026 growth (+12.3%) show the franchise is still compounding, Firefly keeps the product standard current, and buying back shares at ~10× owner cash while FCF grows is rational capital allocation that will compound book value per share faster than the market expects.
most_important_missing_fact: A share-count and SBC bridge tied to cohort net new ARR so we can judge whether buybacks are creating per-share owner value after AI reinvestment and dilution, not just reducing share count.
falsifiers: Annual share repurchases fall below $5B while long-term debt stays above $8B for two consecutive fiscal years
Trailing four-quarter free cash flow per share stays below $18.00 for four quarters
Subscription revenue mix or RPO conversion within twelve months deteriorates materially for two consecutive reported periods
specialist_findings: Buffett/Weschler lens: franchise quality and cash conversion pass; reinvestment into AI is defensive more than clearly NPV-positive on disclosed facts. Component audit: net financial claims correctly small/negative; AI reserve and Firefly optionality are the judgment nodes. Prefer watch over approve until owner-earnings growth is proven net of AI spend and buybacks are clearly accretive on a per-share, post-SBC basis. Do not treat Lawrence synthesis 32% as the decision IRR.
